PullRequest.Title: Add expassigned tag to settings editor to show which settings are actively affected by an exptreatment
PullRequest.Body: Add `@tag:expassigned` allowing users to filter settings with ExP assignments

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup resolves experimental configuration defaults and records assignment membership
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The BlockRestore contribution constructor queues updateDefaults; experimental values must resolve before the default-configuration reload, while assignment-membership publication is joined at the end of processExperimentalSettings. Construction itself remains synchronous. For ordinary enabled configurations, the first non-overridden experimental setting already awaited TAS initialization/initial fetch before this PR, so the new metadata join does not add another startup network barrier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: TAS client initial treatment/assignments fetch, including the assignments endpoint routed through the main-process request service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared initial client fetch in the normal cold-start path; treatment reads then use the initialized in-memory client across the realistically dozens of experimental settings. A client replacement can retry the current read once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: processExperimentalSettings called getTreatment for every experimental property; any non-overridden cold read awaited TAS initialization/initial fetch before defaults were reloaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold value resolution already awaited this fetch before the diff for the first non-overridden experimental setting. Assignment metadata for a developer-overridden setting can also await it, but the complete startup scan ordinarily already reaches the same fetch, so no additional normal critical-path round trip is established.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assignments endpoint request through the main-process request service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Part of the shared initial/refetch operation rather than one independently proven IPC round trip per setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same TAS client setup and initial-fetch transport served existing treatment reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same cold TAS boundary as before for normal startup; the diff exposes assignment metadata but does not prove increased effective startup IPC cardinality after client caching/coalescing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All registered configuration properties are scanned, with treatment work only for the realistically dozens of schemas carrying experiment metadata; cached membership retains at most one key/request token per such property.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Value reads remain sequential in processExperimentalSettings. Developer overrides may launch deferred metadata reads, but normal startup encounters a non-overridden read that awaits the shared client fetch; assignment notifications are coalesced into one event-loop-turn batch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold TAS state awaits the existing initial fetch; warm reads use the in-memory TAS client. The new assignment Set distinguishes assigned and absent membership and is updated only on state changes. Request tokens prevent stale metadata publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path, sequential scan, shared initial-fetch barrier, and final metadata join from changed code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of experimental properties and TAS latency varies by product/window, but no additional normal cold-start boundary or multiplicity was demonstrated after cache sharing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the suspicious Promise.all can wait for deferred override metadata, but the ordinary complete startup scan already waits for the same initial TAS fetch through non-overridden experiments; dynamic single-property publication is not awaited by the registry event source.

Scenarios.Scenario: TAS assignment refetch updates an open Settings editor using @tag:expassigned
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing TAS refetch completes and the configuration contribution re-reads auto/pending settings, membership changes are coalesced to the next event-loop turn. If the assignment filter is active, the editor re-inspects changed keys and performs one search-model/TOC/tree rebuild; otherwise it performs only keyed updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing refetch for the logical assignment update; changed configuration reads use the initialized client cache rather than adding per-setting network requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: TAS already refetched and emitted onDidRefetchAssignments; the diff adds local membership propagation and editor refresh after that boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network refetch precedes assignment-change publication; editor rendering does not issue network, filesystem, database, subprocess, or IPC work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of assignment keys whose membership actually changed, deduplicated in a Set, and size of the current settings search result (up to the settings catalog for a filter-only query).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The configuration throttler serializes refetch processing. RunOnceScheduler coalesces sequential/microtask membership changes into one notification and the editor performs one full rebuild for an active assignment filter, not one rebuild per key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm TAS reads are in-memory. Membership lookups are O(1) Set reads; unchanged positive or negative membership does not emit. The search model rebuilds once because assignment membership changes filter inclusion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the scheduler implementation, 40-key batching test, editor rebuild tests, and changed event handler.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A full filter-only result can contain roughly the settings catalog, but assignment updates are infrequent and explicitly batched; no frame/input-frequency trigger was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: collection-wide UI work is gated to the active new filter and coalesced once per assignment batch; inactive searches retain keyed refresh behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and searching Settings, including toggling the ExP Assigned filter
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Search parsing builds the local result model, each candidate setting is inspected as needed, assignment membership is checked from an in-memory Set, matching rows are filtered, and the settings tree/TOC are rendered. This is synchronous UI/model work but contains no changed remote boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The local search result/settings catalog, with effective cardinality one model element per distinct setting after existing result deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Search/model construction is synchronous on the UI path; assignment changes during focus-sensitive editing are deferred using existing scheduled-refresh handling, and batched membership changes cause one rebuild.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Assignment status is a constant-time in-memory Set lookup. SearchResultModel retains its existing unique-result cache and clears/rebuilds only under existing result changes or the new membership-driven filter refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from SettingsTreeSettingElement, SearchResultModel.updateChildren, renderTree, and focused/context-menu tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalog size and render duration vary, but the added per-element work is a constant-time Set lookup/tag update and the full rebuild is limited to use of the new assignment filter.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the work scales with the existing settings result model and is necessary for the requested filter; no per-frame repetition, expensive boundary, or uncoalesced fan-out is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 19 changed files and every diff page. Traced startup assignment resolution, TAS transport/cache/replacement behavior, configuration reload ordering, assignment lifecycle/coalescing, and settings search/render refreshes. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.
